messages:
maria: Hey team, ran the end-to-end perf suite against the streaming branch. Seeing a ~18% p95 latency regression when partial-decode flushes coincide with batch formation. Logs attached below.

kai: Ugh. Is this the kernel fallback path we saw last week?

maria: Looks related. Profiling shows more frequent kernel switches around flush boundaries. When a partial decode triggers an early send, the next in-flight request gets routed to the small-kernel path even though the batch would have fitted the large kernel after a 10ms coalesce.

sam: Can you paste the hot paths?

maria: Sure. From perf trace (condensed):
```
# perf top (sampled stack)
35%  serve_request -> form_batch -> decide_kernel -> small_kernel_execute
22%  serve_request -> wait_flush -> large_kernel_execute
10%  kv_cache->warmup
8%   schedule_partial_decode
```

maria: Decision heuristic logs: `token_budget_target=48`, `coalesce_ms=12`, `queue_head_timeout=6ms`

nate: So when partial-decode flush reduces the real-time batch tokens, decide_kernel picks the small kernel. That makes sense. But why does it jump kernels mid-batch? We should only pick kernel at dispatch, not per-request.

kai: We do pick per-dispatch, but dispatch gets retriggered on partial-send ack. Could be the preemptive admittance path.

maria: Repro steps: 1) Start 8 concurrent streams (avg 30 tokens each). 2) Every 3rd request hits partial-decode branch (early stop). 3) Batch forms with mixed remaining token budgets -> kernel selection oscillates.

sam: Hypothesis: our token_budget_target is too coarse and doesn't account for skew from partial sends. Need a hysteresis or lookahead: if >X% requests recently used partial-send, bias toward larger kernel for next 10ms.

nate: Or we can delay kernel selection until just before kernel-launch, but keep batch admission consistent. Another idea: pick kernel based on sum of remaining tokens in batch instead of projected per-request token_budget_target.

maria: I tried a quick patch: evaluate `total_estimated_tokens = sum(remaining_estimates)` and prefer large-kernel if total_estimated_tokens > 256. Quick numbers: p95 regression drops from 18% -> 4% in local runs, but mean GPU utilization jumps 6%.

kai: That suggests better latency at cost of slightly higher GPU time. Good trade for interactive SLOs. Any KV-cache side-effects?

maria: We see slightly higher KV cache churn because larger kernels keep longer KV slices in-flight. But warmup improved after 2s steady-state.

perf-bot: Automated regression check: compare branch vs main, p95 delta = -4% (improvement), p50 delta = +2% (worse), cost estimate +3%. See /ci/perf/2467804321.

sam: Let's make the threshold a config flag and run a 24h canary on staging with traffic replay. Also add a metric: "kernel_switches_per_batch" to detect oscillation.

nate: I'll add the metric and a short-circuit: if kernel_switches_per_batch > 1 in the last 1000 batches, fall back to the conservative total_estimated_tokens path.

maria: I'll open a PR with the config, docs, and perf numbers. Also adding a debug trace that prints `batch_tokens` and `kernel_choice` for 1% of requests.

kai: Nice. One more ask: update the inflight admission logic so partial-decode acks don't re-evaluate queue head kernel unless new arrivals exceed batch_min. That should reduce mid-batch churn.
__notes: must be a single continuous string for messages, messages field contains entire thread
